chapter.title: The Professional Journey
chapter.subtitle: Building the backbone of global markets

slides.title: It Started with a Passion
slides.text: Engineering background, fascinated by financial markets from day one. The goal was clear: get as close to the markets as possible.

slides.title: Thomson Reuters — Real-Time Market Data
slides.text: One of the world's largest financial data providers. Working on real-time data infrastructure — the feeds that power every trading desk on the planet. Milliseconds matter. Reliability is non-negotiable.

slides.title: Euronext — Inside a Major Exchange
slides.text: At the heart of one of Europe's largest stock exchanges. Order matching engines, market surveillance, connectivity for hundreds of brokers. This is where you truly understand how markets work — from the inside.

slides.title: Société Générale — The Trading Floor
slides.text: One of Europe's top investment banks. Trading desk infrastructure, risk management systems, high-frequency connectivity. Working alongside traders, quants, and risk managers every day.

slides.title: Brevan Howard — Institutional Hedge Fund
slides.text: One of the world's leading macro hedge funds. Building and maintaining trading systems at the highest level — where every basis point counts and technology is the competitive edge.

slides.question: Why do we run a 'Monkey Test' on our strategies?
choices: To make the code run faster
To prove the strategy beats random entries
To find the best entry timing
slides.explanation: If a strategy can't beat random entries by at least 2x, it means the edge might be an illusion — just noise in the data. The monkey test is a brutal but essential reality check.

slides.title: The Real Edge
